issues.location: design.roles[reaction_match_priya, reaction_match_lukas] facts text vs compiled.bindings/seed_edits
issues.problem: The design's role facts still describe reaction_match_priya as Priya's check-mark on Sophie's checkpoint message (1706012456.000000, C_MODEL) and reaction_match_lukas as Lukas's check-mark on Aisha's dashboard message (1706043661.000000, C_FRONTEND). The compiler silently relocated these to different, previously-unlisted C_INFRA messages (Robert's cloud-bill message 1706067472.000000 and Olena's OOM-eviction message 1706000496.000000) to fix the channel-scope defect from the prior review round, without updating the design's role descriptions to match. Roles message_sophie_checkpoint, message_aisha_dashboard, and message_kenji_tokyo are now orphaned/vestigial in the compiled artifact, no longer serving as reaction targets, which the design text does not reflect.
issues.repair: Update the design.roles facts for reaction_match_priya and reaction_match_lukas (and prune or relabel the now-unused support roles) to describe the actual C_INFRA target messages used in compilation, keeping design and compiled artifacts consistent.

review.rationale: The channel-scope defect identified in the prior review round is now resolved: both qualifying check-mark reactions (Priya's on Robert's cloud-bill message, Lukas's on Olena's OOM-eviction message) and all three negatives (wrong-emoji Priya, wrong-emoji Lukas, wrong-reactor Olena) are now located inside #core-infra, matching the prompt's literal 'In #core-infra, which reactions ... left' scoping without requiring reinterpretation. The focal selector (message_reactions→users[reactor]→messages[authored, restricted to the two known CUDA-identifying message IDs]) is unchanged and remains a faithful translation of the underspecified-mode ambiguity between Priya (confirmed the CUDA limit) and Lukas (first raised it) — a genuine, unresolved choice with no textual tie-breaker. Answer_attributes (message_id, user_id, reaction_type) are real, retrievable columns via reactions.get with no unavailable-timestamp request. Actor U01AGENBOT9's pre-existing #core-infra membership is sufficient for discovery, and the previously-added C_GROWTH membership was correctly dropped as unnecessary. The remaining defect is not a validity failure but an internal documentation inconsistency: the design's role 'facts' text was not updated to reflect the compiler's relocation of the concrete reaction-target messages, leaving a stale description alongside the corrected compiled bindings.
